description:
Analyze all packet capture files in ~/Documents/captures/ to perform passive OS fingerprinting using IP TTL values.

For each .cap, .pcap, and .pcapng file in ~/Documents/captures/, extract every packet's source IP address (ip.src) and IP TTL value (ip.ttl). Aggregate results across all files: for each unique source IP, determine the most frequently observed TTL value (mode).

For each unique source IP, estimate the initial TTL by mapping to the nearest standard default TTL that is >= the observed TTL. Standard defaults are: 32, 64, 128, 255. Calculate the estimated hop count as: initial_ttl - observed_ttl.

Classify the OS family based on the initial TTL:
- Initial TTL 32 -> Windows-9x
- Initial TTL 64 -> Linux/Unix
- Initial TTL 128 -> Windows
- Initial TTL 255 -> Cisco/Solaris

Save detailed results to ~/Documents/captures/ttl_fingerprint_report.csv with columns: ip,observed_ttl,initial_ttl,hop_count,os_family (one row per unique source IP, sorted by IP address).

Save a text summary to ~/Documents/captures/ttl_fingerprint_summary.txt containing:
- Total number of unique source IPs analyzed
- Count of IPs per OS family category
- The IP address with the highest estimated hop count and its hop count value
- The IP address with the lowest estimated hop count and its hop count value
